tagline: The pavement gives out at Tortilla Flat. The road keeps going.
intro: Out of Apache Junction the old road heads into the Superstition Mountains, follows the south shore of Canyon Lake and calls at Tortilla Flat, the last stagecoach stop left on the line. There the pavement quits. The rest is dirt, winding east through the mountains and along the Salt River, past Apache Lake, toward Roosevelt Dam.
The road was cut in 1904 for wagons hauling supplies up to the dam, and most of the way from Fish Creek Bridge to Roosevelt Lake has gone without pavement ever since.

moments.title: Canyon Lake
moments.text: Mormon Flat Dam has held the Salt River here since 1925, the smallest of the four lakes strung along it.

moments.title: Tortilla Flat
moments.text: A stagecoach stop that outlived the stagecoaches, still keeping a post office and a voting precinct of its own.

moments.title: Theodore Roosevelt Dam
moments.text: The end of the line and the reason for it: 357 feet of dam holding the Salt River back as Roosevelt Lake.

practical: Beyond Tortilla Flat the road is narrow and unpaved. It reopened in September 2024 after five years closed by fire and flood damage, and is now open only to high-clearance four-wheel-drive vehicles and utility terrain vehicles.
